How to become a morning person
(for real this time)
Move your wake-up time slowly. Fifteen minutes earlier each week. Big jumps fail, small steps stick and your body adjusts without a fight.
Go to bed earlier, not just wake up earlier. Mornings are won the night before. No phone in bed and lights off at the same time every night.
Give yourself a reason to get up. A good coffee, a walk with music, a workout with a friend. Something you look forward to beats any alarm.
Get bright light right away. Open the curtains, step outside. Light is the strongest signal to your body that the day has started.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Starting with something interesting makes waking up feel worth it.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Starting with something interesting makes waking up feel worth it.

slides.texte_overlay: Prepare everything the night before. Clothes, bag, breakfast. Fewer decisions in the morning means less temptation to stay in bed.
Keep the same rhythm at weekends. Sleeping in until noon on Saturday resets all your progress. Stay within an hour of your normal time.
